EXHIBIT CR 1                   USFWS CRITICAL HABITAT AND U3
  1                I.   INTRODUCTION AND PURPOSE OF CROSS-REBUTTAL

 2   Q.     PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME.

 3   A.     My name is Chris Rowntree.

 4   Q.     ON    WHOSE       BEHALF       ARE     YOU     FILING      THIS      CROSS-REBUTTAL

 5          TESTIMONY?

 6   A.     I am filing this cross-rebuttal testimony on behalf of myself, 3 Trees Ranch Family LP, and

 7          U3 Landowners. U3 Landowners are landowners whose properties are located on, adjacent

 8          to, or in close proximity to Link U3 and who oppose any route that uses Link U3, including

 9          Route 392.

10   Q.     WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR CROSS-REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

11   A.     I respond to testimony urging the Commission to reject Applicants’ recommended Route

12          894 in favor of Route 392 or another route using Link U3. In particular, I respond to the

13          Route 392 and Link U3 advocacy advanced through the testimony of Dr. Mark Turnbough,

14          Dr. Joshua Rhodes, Dr. Andrew Sansom, and the landowners sponsoring or supporting that

15          testimony. I use the phrase “Route 392 proponents” to refer generally to those parties and

16          witnesses advocating that the Commission reject Route 894 and instead select Route 392

17          or another route that uses Link U3. My cross-rebuttal testimony addresses three principal

18          issues: (1) the overemphasis on the Colorado River crossing, (2) Route 392’s inferior

19          performance on key routing metrics, and (3) the site-specific and procedural concerns

20          associated with Link U3.




     PUC Docket No. 59475                                        Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                    1                          on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1   Q.     ARE YOU OFFERING EXPERT TESTIMONY OR EXPERT OPINIONS IN THIS

 2          PROCEEDING?

 3   A.     No. I am not offering myself as an expert witness in transmission-line routing, engineering,

 4          environmental science, electric and magnetic fields, or any other technical field. I am also

 5          not offering legal opinions. I am testifying as an affected landowner based on my personal

 6          knowledge of 3 Trees Ranch and the existing right-of-way on the property, my review of

 7          the Application and Environmental Assessment, and my review of the testimony and

 8          discovery responses filed in this case.

 9   Q.     WHAT IS YOUR OVERALL RESPONSE TO THE ROUTE 392 THEORY?

10   A.     Based on my knowledge of my property and my review of the filed record, Route 392

11          should not be preferred merely because Link U3 parallels an existing 138-kV transmission

12          line near the Colorado River. That theory elevates one feature above the routing record as

13          a whole. The filed comparisons show that Route 392 is longer than Route 894, places the

14          proposed 765-kV line near 51 additional habitable structures, costs $34.3 million more

15          based on the route costs identified by Dr. Turnbough, and depends on late-added Link U3.

16          The EA also identifies Link U3 as crossing the Upper Colorado River USFWS Critical

17          Habitat Unit for a federally endangered species at the Colorado River. Those record facts,

18          together with the property-specific impacts described in my direct testimony, are why I

19          support Route 894 and oppose Route 392.




     PUC Docket No. 59475                                        Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     2                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1   II. ROUTE 392 IS NOT SUPERIOR MERELY BECAUSE IT USES LINK U3 AT THE

 2                                          COLORADO RIVER

 3   Q.     DO YOU DISAGREE WITH THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS’ EMPHASIS ON

 4          THE COLORADO RIVER CROSSING?

 5   A.     Yes. I understand why parties whose property is affected by Route 894 would emphasize

 6          the Colorado River crossing. But a river-crossing argument cannot override the full routing

 7          analysis required in this case. The Commission does not select a route by isolating one

 8          feature, declaring it dispositive, and then disregarding cost, habitable structures, landowner

 9          impacts, cultural resources, late-added-link concerns, and other environmental and land-

10          use impacts along the rest of the route.

11   Q.     IS IT APPROPRIATE TO FOCUS ONLY ON ONE COLORADO RIVER

12          CROSSING WHILE IGNORING THE ROUTES’ OTHER WATERWAY

13          IMPACTS?

14   A.     No. The Colorado River is important, but it is not the only water-resource or riparian-

15          impact issue in this case. The routing record includes many stream crossings across the

16          filed routes. Route 392 has 324 stream crossings in the Applicants’ route data, while Route

17          894 only has 291. That is not a minor detail. If the conservation principle is to minimize

18          disturbance to waterways, riparian corridors, and stream systems, then the analysis should

19          not stop at a single Colorado River crossing selected because it favors Route 392.

20   Q.     WHY DOES THAT MATTER FOR LINK U3?

21   A.     Link U3 does not merely cross the Colorado River and move away from it. That is the

22          critical distinction between Route 392 and Route 894. As I explained in my direct

23          testimony, Applicants’ recommended Route 894 crosses the Colorado River on Link J22


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                      3                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1          at a near-orthogonal angle and then continues away from the River, making its presence in

 2          the river-bottom area comparatively brief and localized. By contrast, every route using

 3          Link U3—including Route 392—crosses the Colorado River and then runs parallel to the

 4          River for approximately two miles before crossing additional riparian features, including

 5          Antelope Creek, Lope-A-Long Draw, and other unnamed streams and springs.

 6                 That distinction matters because the Route 392 proponents focus on only one

 7          feature: the fact that Link U3 parallels an existing transmission corridor at the Colorado

 8          River. But the EA identifies additional facts that materially change that comparison. The

 9          EA identifies Link U3, but not Link J22, as crossing a segment of the Colorado River

10          designated by TPWD as an Ecologically Significant Stream Segment. The EA also

11          identifies Link U3 as crossing the Upper Colorado River USFWS Critical Habitat Unit for

12          the Texas pimpleback. EA at 3-35 to 3-36, 7-3, 7-20, Table 7-4.

13                 Exhibit CR1 shows the result of mapping the Texas pimpleback critical-habitat data

14          alongside Applicants’ publicly available route data at the Colorado River crossings. It

15          illustrates the distinction between the two crossings: Route 392 uses Link U3 through the

16          mapped Upper Colorado River critical-habitat area, while Route 894 crosses the Colorado

17          River on Link J22, which the EA does not identify as crossing that same critical-habitat

18          unit. I am not offering a biological opinion regarding the Texas pimpleback or an expert

19          environmental assessment of either crossing. I am using Exhibit CR1 to illustrate the

20          geographic relationship shown in the publicly available route and critical-habitat data and

21          identified in the EA.

22                 Thus, the Route 392 proponents are not merely asking the Commission to prefer an

23          existing-corridor crossing over a new crossing. They are asking the Commission to select


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                        Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                    4                          on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1          a route that crosses the Colorado River on Link U3 at a location the EA identifies as both

 2          an Ecologically Significant Stream Segment crossing and a Texas pimpleback critical-

 3          habitat crossing, and then remains alongside the Colorado River corridor for approximately

 4          two miles. Route 894 does not present that same combination of impacts at its Colorado

 5          River crossing: it crosses the River on Link J22 at a near-orthogonal angle and then moves

 6          away from the River.

 7                 Put simply: Route 894 crosses the Colorado River on Link J22 and leaves the river

 8          corridor. Route 392 crosses the Colorado River on Link U3 at a location the EA identifies

 9          as both ecologically significant and within endangered species critical habitat, and then

10          traverses alongside the River for approximately two miles. The existence of an old

11          transmission line at the U3 crossing does not make those record-identified impacts

12          disappear.

13   Q.     HOW DOES THIS AFFECT YOUR VIEW OF THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS’

14          COLORADO RIVER TESTIMONY?

15   A.     Their Colorado River testimony is incomplete. It treats one crossing as dispositive while

16          discounting the total waterway picture. A route that looks attractive only because it

17          parallels an existing line at one point may still be worse when the Commission considers

18          the route’s total number of stream crossings, its length through riparian terrain, its

19          construction-access demands, its effect on nearby landowners, and its site-specific

20          environmental sensitivity. Route 392 performs worse than Route 894 on that broader view.




     PUC Docket No. 59475                                       Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                    5                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1        III. ROUTE 392 PERFORMS WORSE THAN ROUTE 894 ON KEY ROUTING

 2                                                FACTORS

 3   Q.     DID DR. TURNBOUGH COMPARE ROUTE 392 TO ROUTE 894?

 4   A.     Yes. His testimony expressly compares Route 392 to Applicants’ recommended Route

 5          894. Several of the figures he identifies demonstrate why Route 392 should be rejected.

 6   Q.     HOW DOES ROUTE 392 COMPARE TO ROUTE 894 ON HABITABLE

 7          STRUCTURES?

 8   A.     Route 392 is materially worse. Dr. Turnbough identifies 85 habitable structures within 500

 9          feet of Route 894 and 136 within 500 feet of Route 392. That is 51 additional habitable

10          structures, or approximately a 60 percent increase over Route 894. Yet Dr. Turnbough

11          dismisses that increase as “numerically insignificant.”

12   Q.     WHY        DO        YOU        DISAGREE           WITH         DR.        TURNBOUGH’S

13          CHARACTERIZATION?

14   A.     Because habitable structures are not an abstract spreadsheet entry.             They are the

15          Commission’s practical measure of places where people live and gather near a proposed

16          transmission line. An increase of 51 habitable structures is not a rounding issue—it is one

17          of the clearest quantitative reasons to reject Route 392.

18   Q.     HOW DOES THAT RELATE TO PRUDENT AVOIDANCE?

19   A.     I am not offering a technical opinion about electric and magnetic fields. But I understand

20          the Commission’s prudent-avoidance policy to concern limiting exposure, with reasonable

21          investments of money and effort, in places where people live and gather. On the record

22          figures used by Dr. Turnbough, Route 392 does the opposite of what that policy would

23          appear to favor: it would place the proposed 765-kV line near 51 additional habitable


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     6                          on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1          structures and would cost more than Route 894. Put simply, Dr. Turnbough asks the

 2          Commission to spend more money to place the line near substantially more occupied

 3          structures. As an affected landowner reviewing those figures, I do not understand how that

 4          supports Route 392.

 5   Q.     DOES ROUTE 392 HAVE A COST ADVANTAGE OVER ROUTE 894?

 6   A.     No. As demonstrated in Table CR 1, Dr. Turnbough identifies Route 894’s estimated

 7          construction cost as $1,680,919,000 and Route 392’s estimated construction cost as

 8          $1,715,218,000. On those figures, Route 392 costs approximately $34.3 million more than

 9          Route 894. A more expensive route may be justified if it delivers a meaningful routing

10          benefit to the public. Route 392 does not. It costs more, is longer, and places the line near

11          51 additional habitable structures.

12




     PUC Docket No. 59475                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     7                          on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1   Q.     DO YOU HAVE CONCERNS ABOUT HOW THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS

 2          USE COST?

 3   A.     Yes. Dr. Turnbough identifies Route 392 as approximately 2.04 percent more expensive

 4          than Route 894, but then opines the actual distinction may be a “preliminary exercise in

 5          false precision.” $34.3 million is real money. It is not insignificant simply because this is

 6          a large transmission project, and it is money that will ultimately be recovered from

 7          ratepayers. More importantly, Route 392 does not command additional cost in order to

 8          reduce impacts near occupied structures.

 9                 Dr. Turnbough attempts to discount the cost difference that disfavors Route 392,

10          while Dr. Rhodes uses smaller cost differences to filter out other routes that disfavor his

11          clients. Dr. Rhodes states that Routes 410 and 416 are estimated to cost approximately $22

12          million to $23 million more than Routes 392 and 402 and treats that differential as part of

13          the basis for rejecting them, even while acknowledging that Routes 410 and 416 perform

14          somewhat better than Route 392 under Applicants’ habitable-structure data.               If the

15          Applicants’ cost estimates are reliable enough to screen out Routes 410 and 416, then they

16          are also reliable enough to recognize that Route 392 is more expensive than Route 894. If

17          they are not reliable enough for that comparison, then they should not be used as a

18          convenient filter to protect Ringler, Solana, Wulff, or other Route 392 proponents.

19   Q.     WHY DOES THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS USE OF COST DATA MATTER?

20   A.     Because cost cannot be minimized when it favors Route 894 and revived when it helps

21          screen out routes affecting the properties of parties sponsoring Route 392 advocacy. If

22          estimated cost is reliable enough for Dr. Rhodes to use a $22 million to $23 million

23          difference to eliminate Routes 410 and 416, then a $34.3 million difference is reliable


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                      8                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1          enough to recognize that Route 392 is worse than Route 894. At a minimum, the selective

 2          use of cost undermines the claim that Route 392 results from a neutral routing analysis.

 3   Q.     DOES DR. TURNBOUGH’S COMPATIBLE-RIGHT-OF-WAY COMPARISON

 4          SUPPORT ROUTE 392?

 5   A.     No. Dr. Turnbough’s own recalculation states that Route 894 parallels compatible right-

 6          of-way for 45.53 percent of its length, while Route 392 parallels compatible right-of-way

 7          for 45.52 percent of its length. Thus, even under his own analysis, Route 392 does not

 8          provide a route-level compatible-right-of-way advantage over Route 894.             It merely

 9          changes which landowners bear the burden while imposing greater cost and substantially

10          greater habitable-structure impacts.

11        IV. ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS IMPROPERLY MINIMIZE LINK U3’S SITE-

12                                         SPECIFIC IMPACTS

13   Q.     WHAT IS THE CENTRAL PROBLEM WITH THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS’

14          TREATMENT OF LINK U3?

15   A.     The central problem is that they treat Link U3 as an abstract line on a map. They emphasize

16          that U3 parallels existing infrastructure, but they do not adequately account for the homes,

17          land uses, terrain, water features, creek systems, access constraints, quarry impacts, and

18          landowner-specific evidence along U3.         Those impacts are not erased by the word

19          “paralleling.”

20   Q.     WHAT OTHER SITE-SPECIFIC IMPACTS DOES LINK U3 PRESENT?

21   A.     Link U3 would bisect 3 Trees Ranch and, based on the route alignment and the EA, cross

22          riparian terrain, cross one of only eight Ecologically Significant Stream Segment in the

23          study area, cross the Upper Colorado River critical-habitat unit for the Texas pimpleback,


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                        Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     9                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1          and bisect the sandstone quarry on Tract 4928.         My direct testimony explains my

 2          assessment of the quarry acreage within a representative 200-foot-wide easement strip. I

 3          offer that testimony as a landowner familiar with the property and its use, not as a mineral-

 4          valuation or engineering expert. These are concrete property impacts that should not be

 5          disregarded merely because U3 parallels an existing line.

 6   Q.     WHY DOES THE EXISTING RIGHT-OF-WAY HISTORY MATTER?

 7   A.     It matters because it shows what can happen on the ground after a line is built. For decades,

 8          the existing 138-kV right-of-way has created practical access and maintenance problems

 9          on 3 Trees Ranch. In steep terrain with creek crossings, draws, ravines, and riparian areas,

10          the utility’s need to access and maintain the line does not stay neatly inside a table cell.

11          The existing line has produced off-easement trespassing, ad hoc access impacts, and

12          repeated conflict over the practical footprint of the corridor. The Route 392 proponents do

13          not adequately grapple with that history when they ask the Commission to place a 765-kV

14          line in the same area.

15   Q.     DOES THE EXISTING LINE MAKE U3 LESS ENVIRONMENTALLY

16          SENSITIVE?

17   A.     No, and I disagree with the Route 392 proponents’ testimony on this point. The existing

18          line proves that the corridor is already burdened. It does not prove that the corridor can

19          absorb a 765-kV line without serious incremental harm. In fact, because the existing

20          corridor crosses creeks, draws, steep terrain, riparian features, and the ecologically

21          sensitive Colorado River environment, the proposed 765-kV line would add major new

22          impacts precisely where access and maintenance are already difficult.




     PUC Docket No. 59475                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     10                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1   Q.     IS THE U3 COLORADO RIVER CROSSING MERELY AN ORDINARY

 2          COLORADO RIVER CROSSING?

 3   A.     No. That is one of the most important points the Route 392 proponents understate. The

 4          U3 crossing is not merely a generic river crossing where the existence of an old

 5          transmission line supposedly resolves the issue. The Environmental Assessment identifies

 6          the Upper Colorado River USFWS Critical Habitat Unit for the Texas pimpleback as

 7          crossed by Links U2 and U3. Route 894 uses Link J22, not Link U3, and U3 Landowners

 8          are not aware of the Application identifying the J22 Colorado River crossing as crossing

 9          that same Upper Colorado River critical-habitat unit.

10   Q.     WHY DOES THE TEXAS PIMPLEBACK CRITICAL-HABITAT ISSUE

11          MATTER?

12   A.     It matters because the Route 392 proponents present U3 as the environmentally preferable

13          Colorado River crossing. That framing ignores the specific conservation status of the U3

14          crossing. Texas pimpleback habitat depends on clean, stable stream substrates and flow

15          conditions. Construction near waterways, access-road disturbance, erosion, sedimentation,

16          and substrate impacts are exactly the kinds of concerns that make avoidance preferable to

17          mitigation. The existence of an old 138-kV corridor does not erase the fact that a new 765-

18          kV line would introduce a much larger corridor and much larger construction and

19          maintenance demands into federally designated critical habitat.

20   Q.     HOW SHOULD THE COMMISSION WEIGH THE PIMPLEBACK ISSUE

21          AGAINST THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS’ PARALLELING ARGUMENT?

22   A.     The Commission should give the critical-habitat issue substantial weight. Paralleling an

23          existing transmission line may reduce certain visual or fragmentation impacts in some


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                        Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                    11                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1             circumstances, but it should not be treated as a trump card when the parallel corridor

 2             crosses federally designated critical habitat and a reasonable alternative exists. Route 894

 3             is that reasonable alternative. It is the Applicants’ recommended route, it avoids Link U3,

 4             and it avoids using a late-added route segment that crosses the Upper Colorado River

 5             USFWS Critical Habitat Unit for the Texas pimpleback.

 6   Q.        HOW SHOULD THE COMMISSION TREAT LANDOWNER TESTIMONY

 7             FAVORING ROUTE 392 BECAUSE IT AVOIDS THEIR PROPERTY?

 8   A.        The Commission should understand that testimony for what it is: affected landowners

 9             seeking to move the line away from their own property.             That is understandable.

10             U3 Landowners are doing the same thing, but with an important difference: U3

11             Landowners’ position is also tied to the Applicants’ recommended route and the overall

12             routing balance. Route 894 avoids U3, was selected by the Applicants as best meeting the

13             routing criteria, has fewer habitable structures than Route 392, has a lower cost than Route

14             392, and avoids the late-added-link concerns associated with U3.

15        V.   DR. RHODES’S SCREENING ANALYSIS DOES NOT SUPPORT ROUTE 392

16   Q.        DO YOU AGREE WITH DR. RHODES’S DECISION TO BEGIN HIS ROUTE

17             SCREENING BY SELECTING LINK U3 AS THE PREFERRED COLORADO

18             RIVER CROSSING?

19   A.        No. That approach assumes the central issue in dispute. Dr. Rhodes first selects Link U3

20             as the preferred Colorado River crossing, which necessarily eliminates Applicants’

21             recommended Route 894 from consideration. He then applies additional screens to narrow

22             the remaining U3 routes toward Route 392. That is not a comparison showing that Route

23             392 is better than Route 894. It is an analysis designed around first excluding Route 894.


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                           Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                        12                        on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1   Q.     DOES HIS PIPELINE-PARALLELING SCREEN PROVIDE A SOUND BASIS TO

 2          PREFER ROUTE 392?

 3   A.     Not based on the support identified in his testimony. Dr. Rhodes states that it is his

 4          understanding that pipeline paralleling is no longer a preferred routing characteristic

 5          because of cathodic-protection concerns related to stray voltage. I do not offer a competing

 6          engineering opinion on cathodic protection. My point is that his testimony does not

 7          identify a Commission rule or order establishing that pipeline paralleling should be used

 8          as the screening factor he applies here. The Commission should not displace Applicants’

 9          recommended route based on an asserted understanding that is then used to narrow the

10          universe to routes employing Link U3.

11   Q.     WHAT IS YOUR CONCLUSION REGARDING DR. RHODES’S ANALYSIS?

12   A.     Dr. Rhodes’s analysis does not overcome the route-level comparison. Route 392 is longer,

13          costs approximately $34.3 million more based on the figures identified by Dr. Turnbough,

14          affects 51 additional habitable structures, and depends on late-added Link U3 with the site-

15          specific impacts addressed in my direct testimony. Route 392 is not superior merely

16          because the analysis is structured to select U3 first and compare only the routes remaining

17          after Route 894 has been eliminated.

18   VI. ROUTE 392 WOULD IMPROPERLY SHIFT IMPACTS FROM ONE GROUP OF

19                                    LANDOWNERS TO ANOTHER

20   Q.     DO YOU UNDERSTAND WHY SOLANA, RINGLER, WULFF, AND OTHER

21          LANDOWNERS OPPOSE ROUTE 894?

22   A.     Yes.   I understand that landowners affected by Route 894 oppose impacts to their

23          properties. I do not criticize them for protecting their interests. But the Commission’s task


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                         Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     13                         on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1          is not to determine which landowner group objects most forcefully. The task is to select

 2          the route that best complies with PURA and the Commission’s routing rules based on the

 3          full record.

 4   Q.     WHAT IS WRONG WITH THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS’ APPROACH FROM

 5          U3 LANDOWNERS’ PERSPECTIVE?

 6   A.     Their approach asks the Commission to protect their properties by sending the line to U3

 7          Landowners. It treats impacts to a large planned development, or to particular ranch

 8          properties on Route 894, as more important than impacts to rural landowners, residences,

 9          working ranches, natural features, guest-ranch operations, quarry operations, and

10          conservation-oriented properties along U3. The Commission should reject that framing.

11          The law does not prefer one group of private landowners over another merely because one

12          group has a different development plan or a different consultant team.

21          AGAINST THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS' PARALLELING ARGUMENT?

22   A.     The Commission should give the critical-habitat issue substantial weight. Paralleling an

23          existing transmission line may reduce certain visual or fragmentation impacts in some


     PUC Docket No. 59475                                        Cross-Rebuttal Testimony of Chris Rowntree
     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                     11                       on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1             circumstances, but it should not be treated as a trump card when the parallel corridor

 2             crosses federally designated critical habitat and a reasonable alternative exists. Route 894

 3             is that reasonable alternative. It is the Applicants' recommended route, it avoids Link U3,

 4             and it avoids using a late-added route segment that crosses the Upper Colorado River

 5             USFWS Critical Habitat Unit for the Texas pimpleback.

 6   Q.        HOW SHOULD THE COMMISSION TREAT LANDOWNER TESTIMONY

 7             FAVORING ROUTE 392 BECAUSE IT AVOIDS THEIR PROPERTY?

 8   A.        The Commission should understand that testimony for what it is: affected landowners

 9             seeking to move the line away from their own property.             That is understandable.

10             U3 Landowners are doing the same thing, but with an important difference: U3

11             Landowners' position is also tied to the Applicants' recommended route and the overall

12             routing balance. Route 894 avoids U3, was selected by the Applicants as best meeting the

13             routing criteria, has fewer habitable structures than Route 392, has a lower cost than Route

14             392, and avoids the late-added-link concerns associated with U3.

15        V.   DR. RHODES'S SCREENING ANALYSIS DOES NOT SUPPORT ROUTE 392

16   Q.        DO YOU AGREE WITH DR. RHODES'S DECISION TO BEGIN HIS ROUTE

17             SCREENING BY SELECTING LINK U3 AS THE PREFERRED COLORADO

18             RIVER CROSSING?

19   A.        No. That approach assumes the central issue in dispute. Dr. Rhodes first selects Link U3

20             as the preferred Colorado River crossing, which necessarily eliminates Applicants'

21             recommended Route 894 from consideration. He then applies additional screens to narrow

22             the remaining U3 routes toward Route 392. That is not a comparison showing that Route

23             392 is better than Route 894. It is an analysis designed around first excluding Route 894.

     SOAH Docket No. 473-26-16349                        12                       on Behalf of U3 Landowners
  1   Q.     DOES HIS PIPELINE-PARALLELING SCREEN PROVIDE A SOUND BASIS TO

 2          PREFER ROUTE 392?

 3   A.     Not based on the support identified in his testimony.       Dr. Rhodes states that it is his

 4          understanding that pipeline paralleling is no longer a preferred routing characteristic

 5          because of cathodic-protection concerns related to stray voltage. I do not offer a competing

 6          engineering opinion on cathodic protection.      My point is that his testimony does not

 7          identify a Commission rule or order establishing that pipeline paralleling should be used

 8          as the screening factor he applies here. The Commission should not displace Applicants'

 9          recommended route based on an asserted understanding that is then used to narrow the

10          universe to routes employing Link U3.

11   Q.     WHAT IS YOUR CONCLUSION REGARDING DR. RHODES'S ANALYSIS?

12   A.     Dr. Rhodes' s analysis does not overcome the route-level comparison. Route 392 is longer,

13          costs approximately $34.3 million more based on the figures identified by Dr. Turnbough,

14          affects 51 additional habitable structures, and depends on late-added Link U3 with the site-

15          specific impacts addressed in my direct testimony.       Route 392 is not superior merely

16          because the analysis is structured to select U3 first and compare only the routes remaining

17          after Route 894 has been eliminated.

18   VI. ROUTE 392 WOULD IMPROPERLY SHIFT IMPACTS FROM ONE GROUP OF

19                                    LANDOWNERS TO ANOTHER

20   Q.     DO YOU UNDERSTAND WHY SOLANA, RINGLER, WULFF, AND OTHER

21          LANDOWNERS OPPOSE ROUTE 894?

22   A.     Yes.   I understand that landowners affected by Route 894 oppose impacts to their

23          properties. I do not criticize them for protecting their interests. But the Commission' s task

  1          is not to determine which landowner group objects most forcefully. The task is to select

 2          the route that best complies with PURA and the Commission's routing rules based on the

 3          full record.

 4   Q.     WHAT IS WRONG WITH THE ROUTE 392 PROPONENTS' APPROACH FROM

 5          U3 LANDOWNERS' PERSPECTIVE?

 6   A.     Their approach asks the Commission to protect their properties by sending the line to U3

 7          Landowners.    It treats impacts to a large planned development, or to particular ranch

 8          properties on Route 894, as more important than impacts to rural landowners, residences,

 9          working ranches, natural features, guest-ranch operations, quarry operations, and

10          conservation-oriented properties along U3. The Commission should reject that framing.

11          The law does not prefer one group of private landowners over another merely because one

12          group has a different development plan or a different consultant team.

13   Q.     DOES DR. TURNBOUGH' S TESTIMONY PROVIDE ANY ADDITIONAL

14          CONTEXT REGARDING THE LATE ADDITION OF LINK U3?

15   A.     Yes. It highlights the practical unfairness of adding Link U3 only after the public-

16          participation process had concluded. Dr. Turnbough testifies that, on November 10 and

17          11, 2025, he and Zach Brady conducted a "detailed reconnaissance" of WulffBluff Creek

18          Ranch with Bart and Fred Wulff"in anticipation of the ONCOR/LCRA filing." I do not

19          fault the Wulffs for investigating the potential impacts to their property. Any landowner

20          who learns that a proposed 765-kV transmission line may cross his or her property should

21          have the opportunity to identify routing concerns, provide site-specific information, and

22          attempt to avoid or minimize those impacts.

  1                  The problem is that U3 Landowners were not given that opportunity before Link

 2          U3 was included in the filed Application. Applicants admit that Links Ul, U2, and U3

 3          were not presented at the public meetings and that landowners along those links did not

 4          receive public-meeting notice because the links were added after the meetings. Applicants'

 5          Response to Julie Williams RFI 1-01 at 2. Applicants' assertion that adding links after

 6          public-participation meetings is "standard practice" does not make the resulting process

 7          fair to U3 Landowners.

 8                  The missed opportunity was substantive, not procedural only. The EA confirms

 9          that, after the public meetings, Applicants and their consultants continued gathering

10          landowner input, conducted site visits and reconnaissance to verify reported constraints,

11          and added, modified, or removed links based on information identified through that

12          process. EA at 2-11, 6-1. Had Link U3 been disclosed during that process, I could have

13          identified the specific constraints described in my direct testimony before the route network

14          was finalized, including the history of off-easement access impacts associated with the

15          existing 138-kV line, the difficult terrain and riparian features along U3, and the sandstone

16          quarry that Link U3 would bisect. Those are precisely the types of site-specific constraints

17          the EA states were evaluated in determining whether route links should be retained,

18          modified, or removed before the Application was filed.

19                  The resulting disparity is significant. By November 2025, the Route 392 proponents

20          had a purported routing expert walking their property and developing a case against the

21          route that would affect them.     U3 Landowners, by contrast, did not learn that their

22          properties were at risk until April 2026 when they received Applicants' mailed notice of

23          the Application. The Commission should not reward that inequity by selecting Route 392
